question: Can simulated Standard Model and beyond-Standard-Model event samples be embedded into one low-dimensional phenomenology space that preserves experimental distinguishability rather than theory labels alone?

key_findings.claim: The encoder maps sets of ten detector-level events into a two-dimensional space using a contrastive same-model versus different-model objective.
key_findings.evidence: Each input concatenates normalized observables from ten randomly resampled Monte Carlo events. Same-model pairs are pulled together, different-model pairs are separated up to a unit margin, and overlapping physical distributions prevent trivial point collapse.

key_findings.claim: For nine gluino-neutralino mass points, the latent space discovers mass difference as the dominant phenomenological coordinate and retains weaker gluino-mass ordering.
key_findings.evidence: Fifty-percent density contours align diagonally by delta-m from 0.2 to 2.0 TeV even though delta-m is not provided directly; a roughly orthogonal trend separates gluino masses despite weak feature dependence.

key_findings.claim: The embedding correctly leaves vector and pseudoscalar dark-matter mediator models largely indistinguishable under the chosen jet-plus-missing-energy observables while separating squark-mediated models.
key_findings.evidence: Vector and pseudoscalar contours overlap across mediator masses because their jets are ISR-dominated; squark spectra vary with the squark-neutralino mass difference and form a distinct ordered region. Pairwise and joint embeddings retain the same relationships.

key_findings.claim: Latent coordinates can be interpreted through binned feature averages, but the learned geometry is partly driven by a small number of obvious kinematic variables.
key_findings.evidence: For combined mediator models, the main vertical coordinate tracks MET and leading-jet pT, while the other tracks second-jet delta-phi and contributes little model separation; the authors note one latent dimension may suffice for the dominant structure.

key_findings.claim: On the Dark Machines subset, phenomenologically similar Z-prime, light-gluino, and stop signals overlap, whereas hard-MET squark and hard-third-jet heavy-gluino signals occupy distinct regions.
key_findings.evidence: The joint embedding of five BSM samples plus Standard Model background is organized primarily by MET and third-jet pT, motivating one representative for the overlapping cluster and a harder-third-jet benchmark to cover a gap.

key_findings.claim: A universal model-space interpretation is not yet demonstrated beyond a small supervised simulation inventory and one signature family.
key_findings.evidence: All case studies use simulated jets-plus-MET events, similarity labels are exact generator model identities, model rates are omitted, and no held-out theory family, detector shift, real collision data, or quantitative coverage-recall target is evaluated.

method.core_idea: Learn a low-dimensional map of theory points whose distances reflect overlap in their detector-level event distributions, enabling visual model comparison and benchmark selection.
method.mechanism: A fully connected encoder ingests small bags of events. Contrastive labels identify whether two bags came from the same exact theory point; a margin loss balances within-model concentration against between-model separation. Kernel-density contours and feature-conditioned bins interpret the resulting two-dimensional geometry.
assumptions: Ten randomly sampled events adequately summarize a model's observable distribution.
Euclidean distance in two dimensions can preserve the distinctions relevant to collider searches.
Monte Carlo simulation and selected kinematic variables faithfully approximate detector-level phenomenology.
Same generator point is the correct positive-pair definition even when neighboring parameter points are effectively equivalent.

techniques.role: Represents a physics model using a resampled bag of detector-level events rather than a single collision.
Pulls together samples from one theory point and pushes apart different theory points subject to distribution overlap.
Summarizes each theory point by a kernel-density region in the learned space.
Colors latent bins by mean kinematics to interpret the learned coordinates.

evaluations.setting: Nine MSSM gluino-neutralino mass combinations simulated through MadGraph, Pythia, and Delphes.
evaluations.metric: Qualitative order and overlap of 50% latent-density contours.
evaluations.result: Contours order primarily by gluino-neutralino mass difference and secondarily by gluino mass.
evaluations.baseline: Direct physical feature distributions; no alternative embedding algorithm is quantitatively compared.

evaluations.setting: Vector, pseudoscalar, and squark dark-matter mediators over grids of dark-matter and mediator masses.
evaluations.metric: Stability and separability of individual, pairwise, and joint latent embeddings.
evaluations.result: Vector and pseudoscalar scenarios overlap, squark models separate by mass gap, and relationships remain qualitatively stable in joint training.
evaluations.baseline: Separate- versus joint-model embeddings and original MET distributions.

evaluations.setting: Five jets-plus-MET BSM samples and Standard Model background from the Dark Machines challenge.
evaluations.metric: Latent overlap and alignment with MET and third-jet pT.
evaluations.result: The map groups three similar signals and identifies separate hard-MET and hard-third-jet regions, suggesting representative benchmarks and a coverage gap.

limitations: No quantitative trustworthiness, neighborhood preservation, calibration, or benchmark-coverage metric is reported.
Training positives use model identity, so physically indistinguishable but differently labeled theories create conflicting supervision.
Only simulated jets-plus-MET signatures and small hand-selected model inventories are studied.
Cross sections, systematic uncertainties, detector mismatch, and real-data backgrounds are largely outside the embedding objective.
Two-dimensional maps are easy to visualize but may hide distinctions needed in a broader theory and observable space.
failure_modes: The embedding may cluster simulator or generator artifacts rather than physical differences.
A dominant variable such as MET can collapse richer multi-observable structure into one axis.
Rare distribution tails important for discovery can disappear when ten-event bags and 50% contours emphasize typical events.
Adding many near-duplicate theory labels can create incompatible contrastive constraints and unstable layouts.
A new theory outside the training support may be placed confidently near an unrelated cluster.
reusable_insights: Represent a generative hypothesis by sets of observations when single samples do not identify it.
Let overlapping observable distributions resist forced separation so model distance reflects experimental distinguishability.
Interpret latent axes by conditional feature maps before using distance for scientific decisions.
Select benchmarks by coverage of observable space rather than popularity of theory parameterizations.
open_questions: Can distribution-aware positives replace exact model identity and yield a calibrated phenomenological metric?
How should theory coverage be quantified with uncertainty, rates, and detector systematics included?
Does the embedding generalize to held-out model families and real collision data?
Can higher-dimensional maps preserve rare-tail sensitivity while remaining navigable for benchmark selection?

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Embedding: Learning the Embedding of the Manifold of Physics Data
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest prior work learning metric-preserving low-dimensional manifolds for collider events and search coverage.
competitive_landscape.difference: Park et al. preserve event-level distances to quantify anomaly-search coverage; this paper embeds bags of events representing entire theory points with supervised contrastive labels.

competitive_landscape.title: Visualization and Efficient Generation of Constrained High-Dimensional Theoretical Parameter Spaces
competitive_landscape.relationship: Adjacent latent-space method for navigating constrained physics theory parameters.
competitive_landscape.difference: That work visualizes and generates allowed points in theory parameter space; the universal latent space instead organizes models by similarity of collider signatures after simulation.

competitive_landscape.title: The Dark Machines Anomaly Score Challenge: Benchmark Data and Model Independent Event Classification for the Large Hadron Collider
competitive_landscape.relationship: Provides the benchmark data and model-agnostic search context for the most complex case study.
competitive_landscape.difference: Dark Machines compares anomaly scores for event discovery; this paper uses a supervised subset to organize signals and backgrounds into a phenomenology map for coverage decisions.

competitive_landscape.title: An Exploration of Learnt Representations of W Jets
competitive_landscape.relationship: Prior interpretability study of latent collider representations and their physical structure.
competitive_landscape.difference: The W-jet study probes representations learned for individual jet classification; this work learns an explicit contrastive geometry between model-level event distributions.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a universal latent space can preserve phenomenological relationships among Standard Model and diverse new-physics theories, supporting discrimination, benchmark selection, reinterpretation, and gap discovery.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Embedding bags of collider events at the theory-point level is a useful shift from event-manifold work, and the examples show sensible geometry. 'Universal' remains aspirational: the evaluation is qualitative, supervised by generator identity, and confined to simulated jets-plus-MET cases without calibrated coverage or out-of-family tests.

reviewer_notes: Read all 25 extracted pages, including the contrastive objective, three progressively larger simulation studies, feature-conditioned maps, conclusions, appendices, and references. Four direct primary arXiv neighbors were checked on 2026-08-23.
